messages:
Maya Patel: Hey team — I'm opening a tiny PR to rework the onboarding tutorial auth pattern. Current snippets use inline keys and `REDWOOD_API_KEY`; we should standardize to `REDWOOD_KEY` in examples and show `export REDWOOD_KEY=...` instead of embedding.

Zack Li: SGTM. Is this just text changes or do we need to touch the sample app?

Maya Patel: Mainly docs, but one sample app (node/hello-world) still has a hardcoded key in example.js. I'll update it to read from process.env and add a short note about using a .env for local dev.

Ravi Singh: Can you also add a curl snippet that mirrors the SDK example? A lot of users try curl first.

Maya Patel: Yep — planning to add both curl and python. Proposed curl:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/ggml-small","input":"hi"}'
```

Andre Morales: Minor nit — our API host for quickstart is `https://api.redwood.dev` in the quickstart (short-lived dev host), not `api.redwood-inference.com`. We should be explicit about which host is for hosted vs private deployments.

Maya Patel: Good catch. I'll keep the examples generic and show both: `hosted: api.redwood.dev` and `production: api.redwood-inference.com`. Add a sentence about private endpoints (customer-specific hostnames).

docs-ci-bot: snippet-lint failed on examples/hello-world/node/index.js: line 12 — detected hardcoded secret

Maya Patel: fixing the sample app now. Changing to: `const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, host: process.env.REDWOOD_HOST || 'https://api.redwood.dev' });`

Sam J: For the README changes, can we also call out the first-deploy checklist? e.g., set REDWOOD_KEY, choose model, and whitelist IPs for private deploy. A 3-bullet list is helpful for new devs.

Maya Patel: Good idea — will add a 'Before you deploy' checklist under Quickstart.

Ravi Singh: Also adding a migration note: older tutorials used `REDWOOD_API_KEY` — include a short 'If you followed old docs' paragraph telling users to rename env var or set both for a transitional window.

Zack Li: Docs CI will want tests for the snippets — can we add a smoke test that runs the curl example against the dev host (mocked)? We already have a harness for that.

Maya Patel: Will add a mocked smoke test under docs/snippets/tests/curl-smoke.test.js. It will assert 200 and JSON keys `id` and `output`.

Andre Morales: One more: update the console screenshot that shows the 'API keys' panel. The old screenshot has the previous UI with 'create token' button misaligned. I can take a fresh capture after the UX tweak next week. Marking as follow-up.

Maya Patel: Nice. I'll merge the text+snippet changes now and leave the screenshot follow-up as a separate PR after Andre uploads the image.

docs-ci-bot: PR #4521 merged into docs/main by Maya Patel (checks: snippet-lint ✅, link-check ❌)

Maya Patel: Link-check failed — one redirect for /quickstart/auth points to the legacy path. Who owns the redirect rule?

Andre Morales: That's on platform infra (I can open an infra ticket). Meanwhile, we should update the link to the canonical path `/docs/quickstart/authentication` to avoid the redirect.

Maya Patel: Done — updated links in two places. Re-running link-check.

docs-ci-bot: link-check passed. All green. :tada:

Sam J: Thanks Maya — tiny ask: can you add a short migration blurb to the changelog so PMs know the env var name change?

Maya Patel: Added a one-line note to docs/CHANGELOG.md: "Quickstart: standardize env var to REDWOOD_KEY; old name REDWOOD_API_KEY still supported for 30 days."

Ravi Singh: Perfect. That should reduce support tickets.

Maya Patel: Closing thread — will watch for any fallout and follow up on screenshot PR. Thanks everyone :heart:
